hints.title: Appended Value Traversal
hints.text: The value is appended to the right of the underlying array. Because it is appended at the very end, it must either become the new root or reside in the right subtree.

hints.title: Root Value Comparison
hints.text: If val is greater than the current root value, create a new root with val, and attach the entire existing tree as its left child.

hints.title: Right Subtree Recursion
hints.text: If val is less than or equal to the root value, recursively insert val into the root right child, assigning the recursive result back to root right.

hints.title: See the blueprint

variables: H: height of the binary tree
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Rebuilding the whole array and re-executing O(N^2) Cartesian tree construction wastes work.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Traversing only down the right spine takes time proportional to tree height rather than tree size.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should recognize that appending to array end only ever affects the rightmost path.
complexity.notes: H is O(N) in the worst case (skewed tree) and O(log N) on average.
